etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin theātricus +‎ -al. By surface analysis, theatre +‎ -ical.

definitions.definition: Of or relating to the theatre.

quote.citation: 12 July 2012, Sam Adams, AV Club Ice Age: Continental Drift
quote.text: The matter of whether the world needs a fourth Ice Age movie pales beside the question of why there were three before it, but Continental Drift feels less like an extension of a theatrical franchise than an episode of a middling TV cartoon, lolling around on territory that’s already been settled.

quote.citation: 1941 July, “The Armistice Coach”, in Railway Magazine, page 317:
quote.text: The ceremony and its scene were characterised by that high sense of the theatrical which has marked the activities of the Third Reich.

definitions.definition: A stage performance, especially one by amateurs.
A commercially produced film to be shown in movie theaters.

quote.text: Release schedules were stepped up so that virtually all of the summer theatricals are coming to video before year's end.

definitions.definition: A person who works in theatre.

quote.citation: 1945, George Tabori, Beneath the Stone, page 177:
quote.text: Both of her parents were theatricals — that is, the father played the violin and the mother attempted to dance but later she dropped the pretence.
